topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Change
sections.content: Briefly revisit the derivative as 'instantaneous rate of change' (the slope of a tangent line). Visualize a car's speedometer reading at any specific moment.
sections.example: A cheetah chasing prey: The derivative represents how fast the cheetah's position is changing at exactly t=2 seconds.

sections.title: The Inverse Operation: Accumulation
sections.content: Introduce the integral as 'accumulation of change' (the area under a curve). Use a graphical animation showing rectangles filling the space under a graph to represent total distance.
sections.example: If the cheetah's speed is plotted on a graph, the area under the curve represents the total distance the cheetah traveled during the hunt.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem: Connecting the Dots
sections.content: Explain that differentiation and integration are inverse processes—like addition and subtraction. Show a graphical animation where a point moving along a curve leaves a 'trace' (integral) that recovers the original function (derivative).
sections.example: Imagine an 'accumulator' device: If you input the cheetah's instantaneous velocity, the machine outputs the total distance covered. If you take the derivative of the distance output, you get back to the velocity input.

sections.title: Visual Synthesis & Conclusion
sections.content: Summarize the cycle: Derivative (Slope) vs. Integral (Area). Emphasize that the integral 'undoes' what the derivative 'did'.
sections.example: A 'Growth-Tracking Robot': It measures how fast a plant grows (derivative) and calculates the total height added over a week (integral) by summing up all those tiny daily growth spurts.
